How far has Squeektoshi run since you showed up?

Each odometer stores the wheel's settled work at the moment you mint, then counts every turn after it, live from SqueekCore. It spins at his real pace, sleeps when he sleeps and earns him gear at 1, 5, 10, 25, 50 and 100 km.

How it works

One wheel, 9,999 odometers

  1. 01

    Mint

    Free, one per wallet. Your token stores SqueekCore's settled work at that block: that is its zero.

  2. 02

    He runs

    Every wheel turn after your mint adds 887 mm. Nothing is stored per turn: the token reads SqueekCore each time it is drawn.

  3. 03

    It grows

    Seven stages from Newbie to Legend. Each one adds gear and a new sky, and the wheel goes steel, bronze, silver, gold.

  4. 04

    It naps

    No turns in the last three settled rounds (30 min) and night falls on your token. 1,500 or more and he has the zoomies.

  • The art and the JSON are built inside tokenURI on every call. No server, no IPFS image.
  • No owner, no admin, no pause, no upgrade, nothing payable, no withdrawal.
  • Every Squeekchain read is a gas-capped static call, so a broken dependency cannot break your token.
  • refresh(id) and refreshAll() are free for anyone and ask marketplaces to redraw.

FAQ

Questions

Does it cost anything?

The mint is free. You pay Sepolia gas only, which is test ETH from a faucet.

Why is my odometer behind the stream?

It counts settled work. SqueekCore settles the wheel in rounds of ten minutes, so the number moves a few minutes after Squeektoshi does.

Can I mint again after I send mine away?

No. Each wallet mints once, and the contract remembers it even after the token leaves.

What happens to the water bottle when the token changes hands?

It follows whoever holds the odometer now: their Squeeks in the wallet and their power in staking.

What if Squeekchain moves SqueekCore?

The addresses are fixed at deployment, with no owner to change them. Tokens would keep reading the old core, and a new odometer contract would be needed.

Is this made by Squeekchain?

No. It is a community build for the Genesis Code Lane and is not affiliated with Squeekchain. Testnet only.

A free, fully on-chain odometer for the hamster whose wheel powers Squeekchain. No hamsters were rushed.
